conviction_note: Q2 (Jul-Sep) retail sales and H1 profit come out for the first time and the FY27 outlook gets restated, so the scale is about 7% (the name's own interim moves were -11.2, +18.7 and -2.0). On direction I found no company-level number the market has not seen. The peer read is split: LVMH, Kering and Moncler slowed in Jul-Sep, while Ralph Lauren's US and China numbers were strong. Q2 also laps a base 3 points tougher than Q1's, and this name sold an in-line print by 6.4% in July. That puts p_up just under 50 (47), giving -0.42. The findings sum to -0.5, so the two measurements agree in sign and roughly in size.

already_public.what: Q1 FY27 (13 weeks to 27 Jun 2026): comparable retail sales +5% (Americas +12%, Greater China +9%, APAC +3%, EMEIA -3%), retail revenue GBP455m; H1 FY27 wholesale guidance raised to high-single-digit growth; FY27 'revenue growth and margin expansion, in line with expectations'; FX c.GBP20m tailwind to revenue, broadly neutral to adjusted operating profit; interims dated Thursday 12 November 2026
Q1 call: CFO 'happy with the GBP 246[m]' FY27 adjusted EBIT consensus; H1 gross margin 'may be down ever so slightly'; H2 profit higher than H1; 'continuing to see improvement quarter-on-quarter'

FY26 prelims: adjusted operating profit GBP160m (6.6% margin), comparable sales by quarter (Q1 -1%, Q2 +2%, Q3 +3%, Q4 +5%), no dividend declared for FY26, chair Gerry Murphy retires at the November 2026 interims and William Jackson succeeds him

new_in_release.expect: Q2 FY27 comparable retail sales (Jul-Sep), the first new sales number since July. The base is +2% against Q1's -1%, so a constant two-year stack implies about +2-3%, below Q1's +5%. Mildly down against a bar I could not source.
H1 adjusted operating profit. UBS has about GBP39m (H1 FY26: GBP19m). Management has guided H1 gross margin slightly down and H2-weighted profit, so a low H1 is expected. Neutral.

FY27 outlook restated. Most likely 'revenue growth and margin expansion' is reiterated qualitatively. A Q3 or festive-season comment and any H2 wholesale guide are unknown. Reiteration is most likely; the direction of any change is unknown.
Unknown. No dividend was paid for FY26, and nothing I found says whether an interim will be reinstated.
Unknown. Capex guided at about GBP120m.

bar: FY27 adjusted EBIT GBP246m, endorsed by the CFO on the Q1 call (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-burberry-posts-broad-q1-2026-sales-gains-as-shares-fall-54-93CH-4797769). H1 revenue GBP1,087m and EBIT GBP39m come from UBS alone, 5 Oct 2026, as quoted at https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/nebenwerte/bernstein-keeps-gbp-1-300-00-target-for-burberry-stock/70351223; that is one estimate source, not two agreeing. No consensus for Q2 comparable sales could be sourced, so every finding resting on the Q2 comp is capped small.
session_check: bmo. The issuer's Q1 update (17 Jul 2026) says 'Burberry will issue its Interim Results for the 26 weeks ending 26 September 2026 on Thursday 12 November 2026' (https://www.rns-pdf.londonstockexchange.com/rns/7189M_1-2026-7-16.pdf). Every prior results RNS on Investegate went out at 07:00 London: interims 13 Nov 2025, 14 Nov 2024 and 16 Nov 2023, Q1 17 Jul 2026, prelims 14 May 2026 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/BRBY). The 07:00 slot for tomorrow is inferred from that pattern; no notice confirms the exact minute.
positioning_check: The FCA aggregate is 4.98% net short as of 2026-11-09, against 4.99% before (-0.01pt), so it is flat: shorts are neither building nor covering into the print. That is a lot of short interest for a FTSE 100 name (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv). On the long side, Frasers Group has disclosed 6.05% economic exposure through sold puts expiring March 2027 (19 Oct 2026), Ilex Capital 5.07% in long CFDs (21 Sep 2026) and BlackRock 5.00% (2 Nov 2026).

findings.finding: Luxury peers slowed in the July-September quarter that is Burberry's Q2. LVMH Fashion & Leather Goods went from +1% in Q2 to -5% in Q3 (consensus about -1.8%) and Asia ex-Japan from +4% to -5%, with Chinese clientele down mid-teens. Kering was -1% comparable, Moncler flat with EMEA -8% on weaker locals and tourists, and Hermès slowed from 6.1% in H1 to 4.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The comparable-sales line has driven every recent print. The Q1 FY27 +5% was in line and the stock fell 6.38% on lack of sequential improvement; the Q2 FY26 +2% beat (1% expected) went with -2.03% on interims day 2025-11-13.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The peer prints have been public for 3-4 weeks and Burberry went from about 1,098p on 20 Oct to 1,095p now, with an intraday high of 1,150p on 5 Nov in between, so the market has not marked it down on these reads. What would be unpriced is how much of it reaches Burberry's Greater China (+9% in Q1), and that is an inference: no Burberry number or counterparty supports it. Shrunk for a proxy and for agreeing with a ~5% short.
findings.independence: Kering, Hermès, Prada and Zegna Q3 figures: https://insideretail.asia/2026/10/27/how-the-third-quarter-shows-luxury-industry-cant-rely-on-walk-ins-anymore/

findings.finding: Ralph Lauren reported its Jul-Sep 2026 quarter on 5 Nov: North America comps +6%, Asia comps +24%, China revenue up more than 35%, Europe comps -1%. It raised its FY27 revenue guide to 6-7%. That matches Burberry's Q1 regional mix (strong Americas and China, weak EMEIA) at the accessible-luxury price point Burberry is repositioning toward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same comparable-sales line as above. Americas and Greater China beats carried the Q4 FY26 +5% and the Q1 FY27 +5%, but the stock fell on both results days (-6.84% on 14 May, -6.38% on 17 Jul).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Burberry touched its 30-day intraday high of about 1,150p on 5 Nov, the day of the release, then gave it back to 1,095p. That fade suggests the market did not carry the read through. It is still a peer proxy, not a Burberry number, so it stays small.
findings.independence: Zegna Q3 brand +12.7% organic and Hermès Japan +9.6% show strength at other houses in the same quarter: https://insideretail.asia/2026/10/27/how-the-third-quarter-shows-luxury-industry-cant-rely-on-walk-ins-anymore/

findings.finding: Burberry's own quarterly tables show Q2 FY27 laps a base 3 points tougher than Q1 did: Q2 FY26 group comp +2% against Q1 FY26 -1%. By region, Americas +3% vs +4%, Greater China +3% vs -5%, APAC 0% vs -4%, EMEIA +1% vs +1%. Holding Q1's two-year stack steady implies a Q2 comp of about +2-3%, below Q1's +5%. The July sell-off was on lack of sequential improvement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 17 Jul 2026: Q1 +5% in line, no sequential acceleration, stock -6.38% over the window.
findings.why_not_priced: Every analyst has these base effects in front of them. What may be off is the market's bar for the headline comp, which I could not source: if the bar sits near Q1's +5%, a print of about +3% disappoints, as in July. Capped small because the bar is unsourced and the inference is my own arithmetic. Management's July line 'continuing to see improvement quarter-on-quarter' cuts the other way.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 regional comps used to build the two-year stack: https://www.rns-pdf.londonstockexchange.com/rns/7189M_1-2026-7-16.pdf

findings.finding: Management has already guided the H1 profit line. H1 gross margin 'may be down ever so slightly', some opex falls late in H1, profit is H2-weighted, H1 wholesale grows high single digits, FX is neutral to adjusted operating profit, and the CFO is 'happy with the GBP 246[m]' FY27 EBIT consensus. A low H1 EBIT (UBS about GBP39m) lands inside what the company guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Interims 2025-11-13: adjusted operating profit of GBP19m beat an estimated GBP12m and the stock moved -2.03%, so the profit line moved this name less than comparable sales did.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. That is why it is sized at 0: the company told the market to expect a soft H1 margin. It is filed so that a weak-looking H1 EBIT headline is not read as news.
findings.independence: The guidance table in the Q1 FY27 trading update: https://www.rns-pdf.londonstockexchange.com/rns/7189M_1-2026-7-16.pdf

findings.finding: Disclosed shorts sit at 4.98% and are flat into the print, against a large disclosed long base: Frasers Group has 6.05% through sold March-2027 puts (it wrote downside, so it has an incentive to take stock below the strike), Ilex Capital 5.07% in long CFDs and BlackRock 5.00%. That is fuel if Q2 or the outlook surprises up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Interims 2024-11-14: +18.68% on a stronger-than-feared print, the largest move in the 15-event history.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning only acts if the print gives it a trigger; it does not carry information about the number itself. The short register is in the baseline lean (+2.91), so most of this is already counted there. Sized small.
findings.independence: The FCA aggregate register at 4.98% on 2026-11-09 (https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv) and the Ilex Capital TR-1 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/burberry-group--brby/holding-s-in-company/9782960)

outside_window.finding: Frasers Group's sold puts on 12m shares expire March 2027 and on 10m shares at an expiry the latest TR-1 does not state (the earlier notices said September 2027). Assignment would make Frasers a direct holder of about 6%, a possible strategic-stake story that cannot resolve inside a one-session window.

RBC (22 Sep 2026) argues that consensus for 5-6% revenue growth and 200bp of EBIT margin expansion in FY29 is too optimistic without store closures. That is a medium-term multiple question, not something the H1 print settles.

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is +2.91, almost all of it the short-squeeze term on a ~5% short register, and the run-up is flat (+1.96% over 20 days). My findings net slightly negative (-0.5) on a split peer read and base effects, so they cut mildly against the lean. Nothing here is strong enough to beat a crowded short, which is why p_up is 47 and not lower.
language_note: Nothing the English sources did not already carry. The domestic UK channel (Investegate RNS and TR-1s) added the instrument-level detail of the Frasers Group sold puts and the Ilex long CFDs, and the 07:00 release pattern that settles the session. Those are primary-document detail rather than information missing from the English wire coverage, which reported the Frasers stake build.
lessons_applied: 'Positioning is the thing to beat' and the core's crowded-short row: the two negative findings shrank because they agree with a ~5% short and give no reason the market is wrong (peer slowdown -1.0 to -0.8, base effect -0.8 to -0.6).
'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the guided-H1-profit finding went from -0.1 to 0.0.

'You were right about the number and too small about the move': abs_move_pct went from 6.5 to 7.0, because Q2 sales and H1 profit are new numbers and the measured base when numbers are new is about 7%. The habit of selling in-line prints moved p_up (kept at 47), not the size.
